sourceDate.text: 唐乾寧三年至周廣順元年

translationRepairs: In the third year of the Zhonghe reign (886), Qin Zongquan of Caizhou dispatched Sun Ru and Liu Jianfeng with ten thousand men under his younger brother Zongheng to seize territory in Huainan, and Yin began as a junior officer under Sun Ru.

In the third year of the Zhonghe reign (883), Qin Zongquan of Caizhou dispatched Sun Ru and Liu Jianfeng with ten thousand men under his younger brother Zongheng to seize territory in Huainan, and Yin began as a junior officer under Sun Ru.
The third year of Zhonghe corresponds to AD 883, not 886.
The court appointed Jianfeng military commissioner of Hunan and made Yin overall commander of the horse and foot forces.
Emperor Xizong appointed Jianfeng military commissioner of Hunan and made Yin overall commander of the horse and foot forces.
僖宗 explicitly identifies Emperor Xizong as the sovereign who made the appointments.
Liu Shizheng, commissioner of Guiguan, grew alarmed and sent Chen Kelin, Wang Jianwu, and others to hold Quanyi Ridge with an army.
Liu Shizheng, commissioner of Guiguan, grew alarmed and sent Chen Kefan, Wang Jianwu, and others to hold Quanyi Ridge with an army.
陳可璠 is Chen Kefan; Kelin is a mistaken reading of the given name.
Guiguan commissioner Liu Shizheng was afraid and sent his generals Chen Kelin, Wang Jianwu, and others to lead troops to hold Quanyi Ridge.
Guiguan commissioner Liu Shizheng was afraid and sent his generals Chen Kefan, Wang Jianwu, and others to lead troops to hold Quanyi Ridge.
The literal field must use the same correct name Chen Kefan.
Yin sent envoys to treat with Liu Shizheng, but when they reached the frontier Chen Kelin and his men refused them entry.
Yin sent envoys to treat with Liu Shizheng, but when they reached the frontier Chen Kefan and his men refused them entry.
The shortened 可璠 refers to Chen Kefan and should read Kefan.
Yin sent envoys on a friendly mission to Shizheng; when the envoys reached the border, Kelin and the others would not admit them.
Yin sent envoys on a friendly mission to Shizheng; when the envoys reached the border, Kefan and the others would not admit them.
The paired literal short form of 可璠 must read Kefan.

Enraged, Yin sent Li Qiong with seven thousand men. They captured Chen Kelin and more than two thousand troops and buried them alive, then besieged Guiguan, took Liu Shizheng captive, and annexed all his dependent prefectures.

Enraged, Yin sent Li Qiong with seven thousand men. They captured Chen Kefan and more than two thousand troops and buried them alive, then besieged Guiguan, took Liu Shizheng captive, and annexed all his dependent prefectures.
The captured general is Chen Kefan, named 可璠 in the source.

Yin was angry and sent Qiong and others with seven thousand troops to attack; they captured Kelin and others and more than two thousand of their soldiers, buried them all alive, then besieged Guiguan, took Shizheng prisoner, and seized all his subordinate prefectures.

Yin was angry and sent Qiong and others with seven thousand troops to attack; they captured Kefan and others and more than two thousand of their soldiers, buried them all alive, then besieged Guiguan, took Shizheng prisoner, and seized all his subordinate prefectures.
The literal occurrence of 可璠 must likewise read Kefan.
After Sun Ru's defeat at Xuancheng, Yin's younger brother Ma Bin fell into Yang Xingmi's hands. Xingmi enrolled Sun Ru's survivors in the "Black Cloud Corps" and appointed Bin its commander.
After Sun Ru's defeat at Xuancheng, Yin's younger brother Ma Cong fell into Yang Xingmi's hands. Xingmi enrolled Sun Ru's survivors in the "Black Cloud Corps" and appointed Cong its commander.
馬賨 is Ma Cong; Bin is a mistaken reading of 賨.
Earlier, when Sun Ru was defeated at Xuancheng, Yin's younger brother Bin was seized by Yang Xingmi; Xingmi took Ru's remaining troops into the "Black Cloud Corps" and made Bin its commander.
Earlier, when Sun Ru was defeated at Xuancheng, Yin's younger brother Cong was seized by Yang Xingmi; Xingmi took Ru's remaining troops into the "Black Cloud Corps" and made Cong its commander.
The literal field must identify 賨 as Cong.

Bin fought under Yang Xingmi with repeated distinction. Steady and never self-aggrandizing, he won Xingmi's affection. When Xingmi asked whose son he was, Bin answered, "I am Ma Yin's younger brother."

Cong fought under Yang Xingmi with repeated distinction. Steady and never self-aggrandizing, he won Xingmi's affection. When Xingmi asked whose son he was, Cong answered, "I am Ma Yin's younger brother."
Every shortened 賨 in this passage refers to Ma Cong.

Bin followed Xingmi in campaigns and repeatedly distinguished himself; he was grave in bearing and never boastful; Xingmi favored him and asked whose son he was; Bin said, "I am Ma Yin's younger brother."

Cong followed Xingmi in campaigns and repeatedly distinguished himself; he was grave in bearing and never boastful; Xingmi favored him and asked whose son he was; Cong said, "I am Ma Yin's younger brother."
The paired literal references to 賨 must use Cong.
賨 is Cong in this short reply notice.
The literal field must likewise render 賨 as Cong.
On another day Xingmi asked again. Bin demurred: "I am only a beaten man from Sun Ru's army. You spared my life; nothing short of dying for you could repay that debt.
On another day Xingmi asked again. Cong demurred: "I am only a beaten man from Sun Ru's army. You spared my life; nothing short of dying for you could repay that debt.
The speaker named 賨 is Ma Cong, not Bin.
Another day he asked again; Bin declined and said, "Your servant is a defeated soldier of Sun Ru; by your grace I was spared death—only giving my life would be inadequate repayment.
Another day he asked again; Cong declined and said, "Your servant is a defeated soldier of Sun Ru; by your grace I was spared death—only giving my life would be inadequate repayment.
The paired literal speaker name must use Cong.
He then sent Bin home with rich gifts and full honors.
He then sent Cong home with rich gifts and full honors.
賨 in the return notice refers to Ma Cong.
He then sent Bin home with generous gifts.
He then sent Cong home with generous gifts.
The literal field must render 賨 as Cong.
Yin was greatly pleased and memorialized recommending Bin as deputy military commissioner.
Yin was greatly pleased and memorialized recommending Cong as deputy military commissioner.
The person recommended as deputy commissioner is Ma Cong.
The Liang founder named Yin Celestial-Registry Grand General. Yin made his brother Bin left chancellor and Xu Cun right chancellor, with Liao Guangtu and seventeen others as academicians.
The Liang founder named Yin Celestial-Registry Grand General. Yin made his brothers Ma Cong left chancellor and Ma Cun right chancellor, with Liao Guangtu and seventeen others as academicians.
賨 is Ma Cong, and 存 is Ma Cun, another brother of Ma Yin. 'Xu Cun' is unsupported and incorrect.
The Taizu appointed Yin Celestial-Registry Grand General; Yin made his younger brother Bin left chancellor, Cun right chancellor, and Liao Guangtu and seventeen others academicians.
The Taizu appointed Yin Celestial-Registry Grand General; Yin made his younger brothers Ma Cong left chancellor and Ma Cun right chancellor, and Liao Guangtu and seventeen others academicians.
The literal field must identify the two brothers consistently as Ma Cong and Ma Cun, supplying their shared surname from Ma Yin.
Cheng pressed the attack on Xizhou. Shichou fled to Jiangzhou and sent his son Shigao with the tribal chiefs to surrender to Liu Cheng.
Liu Qing and the others pressed the attack on Xizhou. Shichou fled to Jiangzhou and sent his son Shigao with the tribal chiefs to surrender to Liu Qing.
The source lost two occurrences of the rare character 勍 during scraping. CText preserves 劉勍 in the preceding sentence and 勍 as both subject and object here.
(Ma Yin entered Hunan in the third year of Qianning (896) and the house endured until the first year of Guangshun (951)—fifty-seven years in all; see the "Chronological Tables" for details.)]〉
